intent: Archive retention guide with a verified ECR lifecycle example

title: Frame retention around the cost of a deletion: a cache miss, not an outage
why: A missing archive means fetch starts a plain JVM (constitution 1 and 3) and the trainer re-pushes it on its next run, so operators can reason about risk as slower starts plus one training run
alternative: Lead with rules and numbers only - rejected: operators could not judge how conservative to be

title: Example policy is count-based (newest N fp-* tags); age-based expiry is explained as unsafe for running releases
why: A TTL counts days since push and cannot know a release is still deployed; a newest-N window at least protects recent builds. The issue forbids implying a TTL protects active versions.
alternative: Ship an age-based example - rejected: deletes long-running releases' archives. Ship no example - rejected: less usable when the format is confirmed

title: Claim only what AWS documentation confirms; list the rest as unverified
why: Policy format, push-time ordering, 24 h timing and the console test run are documented. OCI artifact treatment, re-pushed tags, immutable tags and whether fetch counts as a pull are not, so the guide says so instead of implying safety.
alternative: Present the policy as tested - rejected: not applied to a live repository
